name: Athaiah
overview: Athaiah was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah and lived in Jerusalem. He is specifically identified as the son of Uzziah, marking his lineage within the prominent Judean family. His residence in Jerusalem situates him within the historical and spiritual center of Judah during his time.
namesAndTitles: The name Athaiah likely means "[the] superiority of YHWH," reflecting a theologically significant meaning tied to the supremacy of God. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:4, indicates a name given within the cultural and religious context of Israel, though it was not directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Athaiah as the son of Uzziah, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Athaiah's significance lies in his identification as a descendant of Judah living in Jerusalem, as noted in Nehemiah 11:4. This places him among the post-exilic community committed to reestablishing life and worship in the holy city. His lineage and residence highlight the continuity of the tribe of Judah and the restoration of God's people following exile.
